requirement: The edge device shall detect potholes from its camera and output a detection with a confidence value, without streaming raw video.
The system shall turn each detection plus vehicle context into a Safety Event that conforms to the Safety Event schema.
Each vehicle shall broadcast periodic position beacons (id, time, position, speed, heading, detector-active flag).
The system shall reject malformed Safety Events before any other processing.
The system shall run plausibility checks on each event and reject or downgrade implausible ones.
The system shall protect against replayed events.
The system shall compute a trust weight for every accepted report from detection confidence, consistency, source reliability and freshness.
The system shall maintain a reliability score per source, updated only after confident outcomes.
The system shall merge reports of the same hazard into one logical hazard.
The system shall count vehicles that drove over the spot with the detector active and did not report as evidence against the hazard.
The system shall count identities that move as one as a single source.
The system shall classify each hazard as Suppressed, Unconfirmed, Corroborated, Confirmed or Expired using explicit rules.
The system shall expire hazards whose supporting evidence is no longer fresh.
The system shall record a human-readable reason for every decision, including decisions not to warn.
The system shall warn only vehicles exposed to the hazard.
The alert level shall follow the hazard state.
The driver app shall present warnings visually and audibly, with distance to the hazard.
The real-time decision path shall not depend on the cloud.
The system shall store events and decisions in the cloud for road-segment history and analytics.
The system shall maintain a lightweight Safety Digital Twin of road-segment state.
The simulator shall generate honest, faulty and malicious traffic reproducibly.
The system shall accept vehicle traces and events from files in a documented format.
The evaluation shall compare the engine with two baselines on the same inputs.
End-to-end latency on the local path (detection to warning) shall be ≤ 500 ms median.
Warnings shall reach an exposed vehicle ≥ 4 s before it reaches the hazard at 60 km/h (≈ 67 m).
False-alert rate shall be ≤ 5% of issued warnings.
Consensus accuracy shall be ≥ 90%.
With up to 30% faulty or malicious reports, the false-alert rate shall stay ≤ 10%.
With 10% packet loss, accuracy shall stay ≥ 90%.
Given the same inputs and configuration, the system shall make the same decisions.
Every decision shall be traceable to its input events and the configuration version.
Raw camera video shall not be continuously transmitted off the vehicle.
Every message between vehicles, and between a vehicle and the cloud, shall carry an authenticated sender identity and be integrity-protected.
A new hazard type shall be addable without changing the consensus logic.
Every experiment shall record its configuration, seed and results.
The in-vehicle hardware shall be selected by benchmark: it shall run the chosen pothole detector in real time within the power and cost budget.
The automated test suite shall run in under one minute and cover every Must requirement that can be tested automatically.
A Safety Event shall reach following vehicles within radio range without the cloud (direct V2V), and through a cloud relay when they are out of range.
The in-vehicle unit shall be the single trusted source of time and position (GNSS), and its interface to the mobile app shall define timestamp alignment and behaviour on communication loss.
The in-vehicle unit shall warn its own driver about hazards in its local hazard cache without the cloud or any other vehicle.

The system shall issue warnings only for hazards that require a driver to stop, slow down or change path: raised at least as high as a standard speed bump, or sunk at least as deep, marked or not. Hazards measured below this shall not raise any alert; hazards whose size has not been measured (camera only) shall raise an advisory at most.
Authenticate users before protected functionality.
Enforce Driver, Ambulance, and Administrator authorization on the backend.
Assign each registered device a unique identity associated with an Ed25519 public key.
Use controlled prototype provisioning to register device identity and public key.
Digitally sign hazard reports on the originating edge device with its Ed25519 private key before relay through the phone/backend.
Use deterministic/canonical representation of signed fields (Section 1 format).
Verify the originating device's hazard-report signature at the backend using the public key registered to the claimed Device ID.
Use HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for the phone/app-to-backend IP transport.
Include a unique Message ID (Device ID + boot counter + sequence number) and the signed send time in each message.
Reject replayed or stale messages using a configurable freshness window on the send time and a seen-ID table kept for the maximum report age.
Correlate independent reports of the same physical hazard without discarding their evidence.
Support ACTIVE/REVOKED device status and reject reports from revoked devices.
Validate externally supplied hazard fields and schema.
Protect backend-to-phone/app cooperative-alert transport using HTTPS/TLS 1.3.
Digitally sign cooperative alerts with the backend Ed25519 signing key.
Provision the receiving phone/app with a trusted backend verification key/trust anchor.
Verify backend alert authenticity in the receiving phone/app before display/action.
Reject duplicate or expired cooperative alerts.
Require authenticated/authorized access to protected cooperative alert services.
Apply configurable rate limits to externally accessible/security-sensitive APIs.
Record security-relevant events without logging prohibited secrets/sensitive data.
Only required permissions for users, services, and cloud roles.
No hardcoded credentials, tokens, cloud secrets, or private keys.
Encrypt sensitive cloud/backend data using platform-supported controls.
Local immediate alerts continue without backend/cloud connectivity.
Measure cryptographic/security overhead on the actual target hardware.
Minimize collection, access, retention, and exposure of user/location/device data.
Run security checks relevant to the final stack before deployment.
Use restricted access, encryption, and S3 Block Public Access.
Retain sufficient security evidence without unnecessary sensitive data.
Each direct cooperative beacon must be Ed25519-signed. Receivers verify sender key, freshness, and replay state before use. TLS is not assumed for broadcast.
Dedicated edge devices should use secure boot where supported and accept only authenticated/signed firmware update artifacts according to the selected platform mechanism.
Document provisioning, active use, rotation/replacement, revocation, and response to suspected compromise of device or backend signing keys.
If direct V2V is used, define how receivers obtain sufficiently recent revocation/trust information; offline limitations must be explicit.
Treat physical access to an edge device as a threat to stored keys, firmware, and configuration; prototype mitigations depend on the selected hardware.
Minimize persistent identifiers and location retention. Rotating pseudonymous vehicle identifiers are future work unless implemented and validated with revocation/trust logic.
Detect configured suspicious activity, preserve evidence, alert the team, and support limited response such as rate limiting, WAF action if enabled, or device revocation.
